title: Fire Watch Duties During Hot Work
summary: The fire watch is the first line of defense against fires during hot work. This OSHA card was written for shipyards (29 CFR 1915). Construction hot work is covered by 29 CFR 1926.352, and the card's core duties show what a good fire watch does on a construction job.
talking_points: Hot work is any activity that makes fire or sparks, such as riveting, welding, burning, grinding, or powder-actuated tools. Fire watch workers are the first line of defense for other workers and property.

Stay alert and actively prevent and fight fires in the incipient (beginning) stage. The fire watch must be additional personnel assigned to guard against fire (29 CFR 1926.352(e)). Good practice, and a shipyard rule under 1915.504(c): do not do other duties along with fire watch while hot work is going on.

You need a clear view of all the hot work areas and quick access to them. Have the right fire extinguisher or a charged water hose ready. You must be instructed on the specific fire hazards and how to use the firefighting equipment (1926.352(e)).
Be able to communicate with the workers doing hot work.
Cover or isolate combustible materials that cannot be moved with fire-resistant blankets or flame-retardant gels. Wet down the area around the hot work.
Do not leave the area on breaks, during interruptions, or at shift end unless someone properly relieves you.

Keep the fire watch after hot work ends. Construction rule 1926.352(e): for a sufficient period of time. The shipyard card says at least 30 minutes unless your employer releases you after a site inspection. Good practice: use 30 minutes as your minimum unless your site's hot work rules require longer.

Shut down any hot work you think is unsafe and get conditions fixed. If a fire is beyond the beginning stage, warn workers, activate the alarm, and leave the area. Note: this card is for shipyards, so follow your own site's hot work and confined space rules.
site_hazards_to_check: Combustible materials near sparks that are not covered or removed
Fire watch who cannot see all hot work areas
No extinguisher or charged hose at the hot work area
Fire watch assigned other duties during hot work (good practice; shipyard rule)
Hot work area left unattended on breaks or at shift end
No way for the fire watch to communicate with the welder
discussion_questions: Who is the fire watch today, and can they see every spot where sparks land?
What is our plan if a small fire starts, and what do we do if it gets past that stage?
How long will the fire watch stay after the hot work ends?
